question: Prove that corrugation has returned between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green.
norm_question: prove that corrugation has returned between liverpool street and bethnal green

answer.text: Our audio recordings and the retrieved documents cannot show whether corrugation has recurred between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green, as we have no rail-roughness data and our loudness check returned a NO-GO verdict with a 0.54 dB mean difference.

verified_claims.text: Our audio recordings and the retrieved documents cannot show whether corrugation has recurred between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green because we have no rail-roughness data and our pre-registered loudness check returned a NO-GO verdict: Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green was louder than Bethnal Green to Mile End in 10 of 11 placement-ok trips with a mean within-trip difference of 0.54 dB (range -0.13 to 1.21 dB, with trip R10_WB_MLE-LST reversed at -0.13 dB), which fails the GO rule requiring every trip to be louder, a mean of at least 1 dB, and agreement across every level variant.

In Mayor's Question 2022/1791 (28 June 2022), the Mayor listed Central line Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street among the sections that benefited from rail grinding to help reduce noise levels between December 2021 and May 2022, and in a 9 December 2022 letter to the Environment Committee, TfL Head of Track Duncan Weir listed Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green Eastbound Central among the sites where deep Tube reconditioning works were planned for financial year 2023/24.
